column1: Whisk together the flour, baking soda and salt in a medium bowl. Set aside.
In a separate large bowl, beat the softened butter and dark brown sugar until well combined and creamy.
Add the egg and maple syrup, mixing until fully incorporated.
Gradually add the dry ingredients to the wet ingredients and mix until a soft dough forms. The dough will be slightly sticky because of the maple syrup.
Cover the dough tightly and refrigerate for at least 3 hours, preferably overnight. Chilling helps firm up the dough and prevents excessive spreading during baking.
Preheat the oven to 350°F (175°C). Line a baking tray with parchment paper.
Remove the chilled dough from the refrigerator and let it sit briefly until soft enough to handle.
Divide the dough into approximately 50g portions, making about 14–15 large cookies. Roll each portion into a ball, handling the dough as little as possible.
Place the dough balls on the prepared baking tray, leaving approximately 2 inches (5cm) between them. For slightly flatter cookies, gently press each ball into a thick disc before baking.
Bake for 12–13 minutes, or until the edges are set and the tops appear mostly dry. The centres should still be slightly soft. Avoid overbaking to maintain a chewy texture.
Allow the cookies to cool on the baking tray for 5–10 minutes before transferring them to a wire rack to cool completely.
For the maple icing, melt the butter and maple syrup together in a small saucepan over low heat, stirring until combined.
Remove the saucepan from the heat and whisk in the sifted confectioners' sugar and a pinch of salt until smooth.
Drizzle the maple icing over the completely cooled cookies. Allow the icing to set before serving.
Store the cookies in an airtight container at room temperature for up to 3–4 days.
Unbaked cookie dough can be refrigerated for up to 3 days or frozen in individual portions for up to 3 months.
For the best texture, avoid adding too much flour, chill the dough thoroughly and remove the cookies from the oven while the centres are still slightly soft.
